title: Sixty fps under the horde: the frame at 400 enemies was going to the post chain's fixed per-pixel work, not to the enemies, and two pixel-identical cuts give it back
context: With the wave ramp shipped (2026-09-16-playtest-difficulty-and-rebuild) sector 3's biggest wave runs about 406 bodies at once and the harness had measured it at p50 20.9 ms / p95 46 ms / max 72.7 ms. The owner wants the horde and wants it to play well; lowering sector 3's threat was ruled out. The task was to find where the frame actually goes at 400+ concurrent and fix that without touching a gameplay rule. The 2026-09-13 swarm numbers (505 concurrent at 60 fps, 2000 merged dots under 0.1 ms) were taken in the lab, not on this path.
outcome: MEASURED, NOT GUESSED. Reproducing the benchmark on an idle machine gave p50 17.2 / p95 24.5 / max 44.5 at 406 concurrent (the entry's 20.9/46/72.7 were taken while the overnight build had several sessions running: the machine, not the code, was the difference). A CDP CPU profile across the wave put the whole frame() at 4.25 ms, of which the crowd's simulation (updateEnemies) was 0.34 ms and postfx.render 3.23 ms; the enemy scans the brief named as suspects (gunship breachLoads, gate pressure, laser contacts, radar blips, sector polls) are all under 0.1 ms together. A gl hook that skips draw calls by primitive isolated the GPU side: skipping every POINTS draw (all ~360 enemy draws a frame, two passes) saved 0.5 ms; skipping every triangle and line draw saved nothing; skipping EVERY draw still left 5.2 ms of GPU a frame at dpr 1 and 23.7 ms at dpr 2 - the fixed floor of the bloom chain (two full-resolution scene targets, one of them 4x multisampled, half-float clears and resolves, the mip chain). At dpr 2, the display most owners play on, the 404-enemy frame sat at p50 21.6 ms with 4 enemies or 400. THE CHANGES, all in src/postfx.js and all output-identical: (1) applyWeights visited every object in the scene each frame and did nothing for the ungrouped ones, and ran the material-conflict tripwire every frame; with the default weight at 1 it now iterates the weight map, and the tripwire runs once a second (0.43 -> 0.09 ms a frame). (2) Each of the two RenderPasses walked scene.updateMatrixWorld again with nothing moved between them; render() updates once and holds scene.matrixWorldAutoUpdate off only across the two passes. (3) EffectComposer's RenderPass draws into the read buffer (renderTarget2) and never swaps, so the final composer's renderTarget1 only ever receives full-screen shader passes; it no longer carries 4x MSAA or a depth buffer (a fully covered pixel resolves to its one fragment). (4) UnrealBloomPass's closing additive blend back into its buffer is read by nothing (postfx takes the pure bloom from renderTargetsHorizontal[0]); its material is not drawn. RESULT: the fixed GPU floor 5.2 -> 3.8 ms at dpr 1 and 23.7 -> 13.3 ms at dpr 2; the dpr-2 frame at 404 enemies 21.6 -> 16.7 ms p50 (p95 23.2 -> 17.8); CPU frame() 4.25 -> 3.37 ms; at dpr 1 the frame was already vsync-bound and stays at p50 16.7-17.3. No gameplay rule, number or pixel changed; src/td-tab.js untouched at 13,505 lines. WHAT IS STILL HOT: three.js's per-object submission for two passes (~2.1 ms CPU at 400 bodies: renderObjects 0.93, updateMatrixWorld 0.52, projectObject 0.47, setProgram 0.41) - the only remaining crowd-scaling cost, answerable by an instanced swarm with per-instance tint/opacity attributes (src/fx/dot-swarm.js, 2026-09-14-dots-not-draw-calls) but not justified at these numbers; the post chain's remaining floor (13.3 ms at dpr 2: the weighted scene rendered at full device resolution only to be halved by the luminosity pass, the MSAA scene target's clear and resolve) which can only come down by changing the look (bloom scale 0.5 on desktop as the phone tier does, MSAA 2x); the breach dive shot, which renders the sinkhole close up at 5M triangles and ran 25 ms a frame at dpr 1 and 93 ms at dpr 2 in these runs, unrelated to the horde; and the wave's spawn-in, where 400 bodies built over 3.2 s put the p95 of the first twelve seconds at 22-29 ms (the harness's stock window measures that, the steady state after it holds p95 18-19).
alternatives: Hoisting the per-frame enemy scans into one shared pass or bucketing enemies spatially (gunship breachLoads, tickGate, laser candidates, radar blips): not done - the profile puts all of them under 0.1 ms a frame at 400 bodies; the change would add code for no measurable gain.
Striding low-priority per-enemy work across frames: not done, updateEnemies is 0.34-0.42 ms a frame in total.

Merging the crowd into the instanced dot swarm: not done. The 2026-09-14 lab measurement already showed draw calls are not the wall, and this profile agrees (skipping every enemy draw saves 0.5 ms of GPU); the CPU submission it would remove is ~2 ms, at the price of per-instance tint and opacity attributes and every material call site in td-tab.js.
Lowering the desktop bloom scale to 0.5 or MSAA to 2x: would take most of the remaining dpr-2 floor but changes the picture; left for the owner to decide with the numbers in hand.
Rendering the weighted bloom-source scene at half resolution: the same trade, the bloom of thin bright lines would soften; not done.
evidence: BEFORE, stock: scripts/browser-lock.sh node scripts/browser-test.mjs --waves --last: 406 concurrent, p50 17.2 p95 24.5 max 44.5 over 657 frames (idle machine; the entry's 20.9/46/72.7 over 474 frames was a loaded one).
AFTER, stock, same command: 406 concurrent, p50 17.3 p95 22.7 max 52 over 660 frames.

artifacts/qa/horde-bench.mjs (CDP Profiler across the wave, before/after): frame() 4.25 -> 3.37 ms a frame; postfx.render 3.23 -> 2.21; applyWeights 0.43 -> 0.09; updateEnemies 0.34 / 0.42; the harness's own state() poll costs 1.2-1.5 ms a frame of what the benchmark reports. Top self-time both runs: (idle), the harness's state(), (program), projectObject/updateMatrixWorld/multiplyMatrices/renderBufferDirect.
artifacts/qa/horde-split2.mjs (gl draw hook, dpr 1): loaded 404 alive p50 16.7 p95 18.1, gpu 9.5-10.3 ms; no points draws 9.8; no triangle/line draws 11.6; NO draws 5.2 -> after 3.8 ms.
artifacts/qa/horde-split2.mjs --dpr=2: BEFORE loaded 404 alive p50 21.6 p95 23.2, gpu 27.4, no draws 23.7 ms; AFTER loaded p50 16.7-17.2 p95 17.8-18.4, gpu 17.9-18.3, no draws 13.3 ms.
Quiet window in every split run was the breach dive shot (state().shot === 'breach'): 5M triangles at 25 ms a frame (dpr 1) and 93 ms (dpr 2), 32 alive.
npm test: 120 test programs passed. npm run check: architecture, line budgets and top-level placement hold; src/td-tab.js unchanged at 13,505.
Browser suites after the change through the lock: --waves --last PASS waves-pile; --sectors 11 PASS lines through sectors-sector-2-debrief; --defense 11 PASS lines through defense-part-dropped.
